findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type and collides on id 0
findings.body: Check builds the denial-cache key only from namespace, raw subject id, action, name, and parent. Identity type is dropped, unlike the positive permission cache, which uses a separate anonymousPermCacheKey. In this service anonymous subjects are "anonymous:0" and the renderer is "render:0", so both have UserUID "0" and share one denial entry. A denied anonymous dashboards:read Check therefore writes a 30s denial that the next renderer Check for the same name/folder hits immediately and returns Allowed=false, never applying the renderer's static read-all grant. The reverse also holds for actions the renderer is denied. Unrelated identities can force false 403s on each other for shortCacheTTL.

findings.title: Denial cache overrides fresher permission data for 30s
findings.body: A denial-cache hit returns Allowed=false before the permission cache or the database is consulted, and a DB deny at the end of Check stores that denial for shortCacheTTL (30s) with no invalidation. The new fall-through reloads permissions and overwrites permCache when some other resource is missing, and List will authorize from that updated map, but a later Check of the previously denied resource still short-circuits on the denial entry. A creator Check that races the permission insert, a grant after a deny, or an inherited allow that only works once the folder tree cache refreshes therefore stays denied for up to 30s even after this process already has an allow in permCache. Denials also freeze the result of getUserPermissions, which still uses the 30s basic-role and team caches, so a role or team change can remain denied after those caches expire.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not actually grant the cached permission
findings.body: "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" says the permission cache allows dash1 so the deny can only come from the denial entry, but it stores map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats a false value as no grant, and this subtest never installs a permission store result that would allow dash1, so the DB fall-through also denies. The test passes if the denial-cache short-circuit is removed. Store true for that scope (and a store grant) so the test fails unless the denial cache is what forced Allowed=false.
